A Family Tradition of Regenerative Stewardship

With four generations working side by side, our family has spent over 20 years devoted to regenerative farming that conserves the land. Each of us plays a vital role in caring for the soil, animals, and community, creating a lasting legacy of sustainability for future generations.

Our Philosophy
Cumberland Folk School at Sequatchie Cove

Join us at Cumberland Folk School to learn hands-on skills and connect with the land. From regenerative farming to traditional crafts, we offer classes that bring people and nature together.

Wholesome, Grass-Fed Goodness—From Our Pasture to Your Plate
Shop Our Beef
What Makes Our Beef Special?

At Sequatchie Cove, our cows live the way nature intended—grazing freely in the fresh East Tennessee air. By raising our South Poll and Angus cattle on a natural diet of grass, we improve the health of the land and produce beef that's rich in flavor and nutrients. We never use steroids, antibiotics, or hormones, so you can enjoy each bite knowing it’s as pure and wholesome as it gets.

Healthy Cattle, Healthy Land, Wholesome Beef
A Slow Process,
Worth the Wait.

Good things take time, and we believe in doing things the old-fashioned way. Each cow takes 2 to 3 years to reach maturity, after which the meat is carefully dry-aged and hand-butchered by Mcbride Meats in New Hope, TN. This slower, more thoughtful process enhances both the flavor and tenderness of the beef, offering you a meal that’s truly a cut above.

Our Partner in Quality:
Manderley Farms

We’ve teamed up with Manderley Farms in Pikeville, TN, to supplement our Grass-Fed Beef supply. Their commitment to daily pasture rotation on high-energy forage aligns with our values, ensuring you receive high-quality, ethically raised beef.

Learn More
A Family Tradition on Every Plate.

We’re a small, family-run farm, and every decision we make is with our community and the land in mind. From the fields to your table, we’re proud to share the fruits of our hard work. Our grass-fed beef is available in limited quantities, so visit us at the farm’s Trading Post on Saturdays to bring home a true taste of Sequatchie Cove.

Pasture Raised Eggs
Hand-gathered from free-roaming hens, nurtured on fresh pastures for flavor you can trust
Buy Our Eggs
Wright Eggs for the Right Reasons

Our “Wright Eggs” are crafted with purpose and care. Raised on fresh pasture, nourished with by hand with feed, and gathered daily by a dedicated crew, each egg reflects our commitment to quality, sustainability, and ethical farming. When you choose Wright Eggs, you’re choosing wholesome flavor and a farm-to-table experience rooted in the best practices- these are truly the Wright Eggs for the Wright Reasons.

Free to roam, bringing pasture freshness to your plate
A Day in the Life of a Happy Hen

Our hens start each day at first light, scratching, pecking, and investigating their surroundings. By mid-morning, most of the day’s eggs are laid—around 3,000 eggs daily! Our crew, from Kelsey and Ashley to farm hands and family, gather these fresh treasures every day, ensuring a steady supply for markets and restaurants near and far.

Protected by Paws & Pasture

With open-air coops and acres of fresh pasture, our hens are free to roam, all thanks to their dedicated guardians—our livestock dogs. These watchful protectors allow the hens to forage safely day and night, guarding against any unwanted visitors that might fancy a chicken sandwich.

 

Farm-Fresh Flavor, Delivered to You

When you enjoy a Sequatchie Cove egg, you’re tasting the “whole karma” of a hen’s natural life—from sunrise scratching to sunset roosting. These eggs, packed with the flavors of the field, are available at our Trading Post, Online, Main Street Farmer’s Market, and dozens of local stores and restaurants from Chattanooga to Nashville. Enjoy every bite knowing it’s farm-to-table freshness at its best.

Our History of Pasture-Raised Poultry

At Sequatchie Cove Farm, our pasture-raised chickens roam freely under the wide Tennessee sky, foraging on fresh grasses and basking in the sunshine. For over 25 years, our family has raised chickens with care, using regenerative practices that nourish the land and produce nutrient-dense, flavorful chicken for your table. From our 300-acre farm nestled along the Little Sequatchie River, we’re proud to share the fruits of our labor with our community.

Locally raised on fresh pasture
Available at the
Farm Trading Post

Our Pasture Raised Chicken is available at our farm’s Trading Post every Saturday from 9–12 Central. Visit us to enjoy the great quality you’ve come to expect from Sequatchie Cove Farm.

Heritage Pork

Shop Our Pork
Our Approach to Sustainable Pork

Sequatchie Cove Farm proudly raises a diverse range of heritage breeds, including Gloucestershire Old Spots, Mulefoot, Large Black, and Red Wattle pigs. By keeping production on a small scale of around ten pigs per year, we prioritize both the well-being of our land and the exceptional quality of our pork.

Rooted in Tradition, Raised for Exceptional Flavor
Fresh Pasture &
Woodland Fed

Our pigs enjoy a varied diet of pasture grasses, foraged nuts like acorns, hickory, and walnuts, along with treats of cracked eggs and seasonal persimmons. We supplement their natural foraging with feed, to provide balanced nutrition for healthy, flavorful pork.

Our Partner in Quality:
Manderley Farms

We’ve teamed up with Manderley Farms in Pikeville, TN, to supplement our Heritage Pork supply. Their commitment to raising their pork in forest environments with room to forage aligns with our values, ensuring you receive high-quality, ethically raised pork.

Learn More
Caring for the Land, Honoring the Animal

With only 90 acres of pasture, we focus on small-scale, respectful animal husbandry, letting pigs roam freely in pasture and woodland areas under open skies. Every pig is hand-tended, reflecting our dedication to humane farming, ensuring they experience fresh air, sunshine, and the opportunity to forage and thrive naturally.

Katahdin Lamb
Tender, pasture-raised lamb from hardy Katahdin Hair Sheep
Buy Our Lamb
The Unique Katahdin Breed

We proudly raise Katahdin Hair Sheep, the only sheep bred in North America specifically for high-quality meat in humid climates like ours. These hardy sheep thrive on our pastures, naturally adapting to the land and requiring minimal intervention beyond the care and protection provided by our shepherds and guard dogs.

Pasture-raised, naturally hardy, and full of flavor
Pasture-Raised
with Natural Practices

At Sequatchie Cove, we mimic nature by feeding our sheep only the native grasses and shrubs that grow in the area. Each day, the sheep are rotated to fresh pastures alongside our cattle, enriching both the land and the quality of the meat, while avoiding any growth hormones, antibiotics, or feedlot confinement.

From Farm to
Table with Care

Our lambs are processed at 8 to 12 months of age at a family-owned USDA facility in South Pittsburg, TN, ensuring a high-quality product with local roots. Every step, from careful pasture management to humane processing, reflects our commitment to delivering healthy, flavorful lamb for your table.

SEPTEMBER
Build a (Cumberland) Foot Stool with Tyler Rogers
September 19, 2026

Join Tyler Rogers for a 1-day woodworking workshop. Each student will learn some basic chair-making techniques while building a 3-leg wooden footstool using mostly hand tools.

26
SEPTEMBER
Appalachian Floor Brooms with Ali Davenport
September 26, 2026

Welcome in the fall equinox while creating a daily use heirloom! Binding together local broomcorn from Sequatchie Cove and a hand carved broom handle from Tennessee Chairmaker Tyler Rogers, you’ll feel the connection to the materials used for generations.

27
SEPTEMBER
Reading the Woods: Tree ID and Plant Ecology of the Sequatchie Valley with Cooper Breeden
September 27, 2026

Join botanist Cooper Breeden on a jaunt through the woods to learn about the plants that call the Sequatchie Valley home and the stories they tell us. The primary focus of the class will be the identification of woody plants (trees, shrubs, and vines).

03
OCTOBER
Stained Glass Stars with Tammy O'Connor
October 03, 2026

Learn the basics of Tiffany method stained glass techniques to make a 3 dimensional glass star, perfect to celebrate the holidays or to give as a most welcomed present.

03
OCTOBER
Dances from Around the World with Anna Claire Camp
October 03, 2026

We will learn fun community dances from around the world such as clapping dances from Russia & Germany and group dances from Scotland & Denmark along with Folk dances from the Appalachian region.

17
OCTOBER
October Fundraiser Event
October 17, 2026

Join us for a causal evening at Sequatchie Cove Farm to celebrate and support us as we transition to a non-profit and grow our offerings! Come enjoy music by Stones River Reelers and a causal farm-to-table dinner.
